question.prompt:
Points \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) on a circle of radius \(r\) are situated so that \(AB=AC,\) \(AB\gt r,\) and the length of minor arc \(\overset{\frown}{BC}\) is \(r.\) If angles are measured in radians, then \(\frac{AB}{BC}=\)

[Figure 1](figures/1994_AMC_12_Q29_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The arc length determines an angle, and the equal sides let us turn that angle into a right-triangle ratio. Since the circle has radius \(r>0\), the central angle subtending minor arc \(BC\) is
\[
\theta=\frac{\text{arc length}}{r}=\frac rr=1
\]
in radians.

First determine which arc contains \(A\). If \(A\) were on the minor arc, the equal chords \(AB=AC\) would divide that arc into equal subarcs. Each would have length \(r/2\). A chord is shorter than its corresponding arc, giving \(AB<r/2<r\), contrary to \(AB>r\). Thus \(A\) lies on the major arc, and the inscribed angle theorem gives
\[
\angle BAC=\frac12\theta=\frac12.
\]
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(BC\). In the isosceles triangle \(ABC\), the median \(AM\) is also an altitude and an angle bisector. Consequently, \(BM=BC/2\), \(\angle BAM=1/4\), and triangle \(ABM\) is right. Therefore
\[
\sin\frac14=\frac{BM}{AB}=\frac{BC}{2AB}.
\]
Since \(1/4\) is an acute angle, its sine is positive, so division is valid. Using \(\csc t=1/\sin t\), we obtain
\[
\boxed{\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{1}{2\sin(1/4)}=\frac12\csc\frac14},
\]
which is choice A.
solutions.title: Bisect the isosceles triangle
